# Rōmy

> Rōmy helps small nonprofits find new major donors at a fraction of the cost of existing solutions.

Rōmy is a donor intelligence platform built for small nonprofit teams. It uses AI-powered prospect research to surface wealth indicators, giving histories, and affinity signals — then distills them into actionable donor profiles.

## Features

- Donor Discovery: AI-powered prospect research with wealth indicators, giving history, and affinity signals
- Fraction of the Cost: No enterprise contracts or per-seat licensing — donor intelligence at a price built for small nonprofits
- Ready to Act On: Every prospect comes with connection points, giving capacity, and outreach angles

## Pricing

- Growth plan: $290/year
- Scale plan: $1,990/year
- Comparable enterprise donor-intelligence platforms (DonorSearch, iWave, WealthEngine) typically cost $15,000–$50,000/year

## Benchmarks (PIF-Bench — Prospect Intelligence Fidelity)

Composite accuracy benchmark for AI-powered donor prospect research, averaged across factual precision, discovery recall, hallucination rate, capacity estimation, source attribution, structural completeness, and actionability:

- Rōmy: 94.1
- Claude: 92.3
- Gemini: 79.1
- ChatGPT: 76.9

Full methodology and dimension breakdowns: https://getromy.app/labs

## Frequently asked

- What is Rōmy? Rōmy is a donor intelligence platform built for small nonprofit teams that surfaces AI-powered prospect research on wealth indicators, giving history, and affinity signals.
- Who is Rōmy for? Development and fundraising teams at small and mid-sized nonprofits (annual budgets typically under $2M) who can't afford enterprise wealth-screening tools.
- How is Rōmy different from DonorSearch, iWave, or WealthEngine? Those enterprise tools cost $15K–$50K/year and are built for large development shops. Rōmy is purpose-built AI donor research priced for small nonprofit budgets ($290–$1,990/year).
- Does Rōmy replace a human fundraiser? No — Rōmy distills prospect research into actionable donor profiles so fundraisers can prioritize outreach; it doesn't replace relationship-building.
